features.title: ACP server bridge

acceptance_evidence.required: ACP stdio tests cover initialize, session lifecycle, prompts, cancel, streaming, modes, and permissions.

known_differences: Interoperability is exercised against a local pure-Rust ACP fixture rather than an external third-party agent.
The bounded bidirectional JSON-RPC peer is maintained in this crate instead of delegating transport behavior to an ACP runtime SDK.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements the ACP stdio server bridge, request dispatch, lifecycle methods, streaming, cancellation, modes, and permissions.
Implements bounded newline-delimited bidirectional JSON-RPC framing and connection-wide failure propagation.

features.title: ACP debug client

acceptance_evidence.required: The Rust debug client negotiates and exercises the pinned ACP bridge lifecycle.

known_differences: Interoperability is exercised against a local pure-Rust ACP fixture rather than an external third-party agent.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements protocol negotiation, session lifecycle, prompt streaming, cancellation, permission handling, and subprocess-tree supervision.

features.title: ACPX harness runtime

acceptance_evidence.required: Harness aliases, permissions, process leases, turns, and optional MCP bridges pass compatibility tests.

known_differences: Harness subprocess interoperability is exercised with local pure-Rust fixtures; durable session and lease storage depends on the injected store implementations.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements harness aliases, fail-closed permissions, process leases, persistent and one-shot turns, and optional MCP bridge conversion.

features.title: MCP stdio server

acceptance_evidence.required: MCP initialize, list, call, resource, shutdown, and process-tree cleanup tests pass.

known_differences: Protocol interoperability is exercised against a local pure-Rust MCP subprocess fixture and never contacts a third-party MCP service.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements the GTA-Claw MCP server handler for negotiated tools, resources, prompts, sampling, notifications, and cancellation.
Implements bounded partial-read-safe newline-delimited JSON-RPC transport and whole-connection cancellation.

features.title: MCP client transports

acceptance_evidence.required: Stdio, SSE, and streamable-HTTP client transport tests pass.

known_differences: Transport interoperability is exercised only with local pure-Rust MCP fixtures; tests never contact real third-party MCP endpoints.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements capability-discovering MCP clients, request deadlines, stdio supervision, notifications, sampling, and shutdown.
Implements the bounded Hyper and ring-Rustls HTTP connector with credential-safe proxy routing.
Implements legacy SSE endpoint discovery, event-ID reconnection, authenticated GET and POST, and bounded retries.

features.title: MCP OAuth

acceptance_evidence.required: OAuth metadata, login, refresh, storage, logout, and bearer injection tests pass.

known_differences: OAuth flows are exercised only against local pure-Rust authorization fixtures and never contact real authorization or MCP services.
OAuth secure persistence is a port; at-rest security depends on the injected platform token-store implementation.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, dynamic registration, PKCE, exchange, serialized refresh, origin-bound bearer injection, logout, and redacted token-store ports.

features.title: MCP server registry
known_differences: Registry lifecycle interoperability is exercised with local pure-Rust child servers; durable configuration and platform authentication depend on injected store and auth ports.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements persistent configuration, discovery, health, probe, doctor, tools, authentication delegation, and managed server lifecycle operations.

features.title: MCP conversation projection

acceptance_evidence.required: Conversation list/read/send, live event, attachment, and approval projection tests pass.

known_differences: Projection fidelity is validated against the frozen upstream shapes through a local gateway backend port rather than a live external Gateway.

implementation_pointers.note: Implements exact conversation list, read, send, live-event, attachment, and approval projection over the GTA-Claw gateway port.

features.title: OpenAI Chat Completions

acceptance_evidence.required: JSON and SSE /v1/chat/completions golden tests match pinned request, stream, usage, and error contracts.

known_differences: Request, JSON response, SSE framing, usage accounting and the error contract are proven against a deterministic runtime double; no upstream OpenAI client library is replayed against the surface.

features.title: OpenResponses API

acceptance_evidence.required: JSON and SSE /v1/responses golden tests match pinned item, event, tool, usage, and error contracts.

known_differences: Item, event, tool-call, usage and error contracts are proven against a deterministic runtime double; the pinned event list is the sequence this server emits rather than a recording of upstream traffic.

features.title: OpenAI-compatible models API

acceptance_evidence.required: List and retrieve model endpoint tests match pinned filtering, identifiers, and errors.

known_differences: List, retrieve, identifier encoding and both error shapes are proven; the advertised set belongs to the test runtime, so this pins the endpoint contract rather than the production catalog.

features.title: OpenAI-compatible embeddings API

acceptance_evidence.required: Embedding request, provider policy, dimensions, usage, and error fixtures pass.

known_differences: Request shape, provider policy, dimensions and error classification are proven against pinned fixtures. Usage is not proven as real accounting: prompt_tokens and total_tokens are hard-coded to zero and the test pins that constant rather than showing usage follow the provider.

features.title: OpenClaw tools invoke HTTP API

acceptance_evidence.required: Authenticated /tools/invoke schema, policy, result, and error tests pass.

known_differences: Authentication, schema validation, scope policy, the success result with its lowered invocation context and the error mapping are proven against a deterministic runtime double.

features.title: Chrome extension relay and CDP bridge

acceptance_evidence.required: MV3 pairing, relay auth, WebSocket subprotocol, CDP target, screenshot, and disconnect tests pass.

known_differences: Pairing, subprotocol and origin authentication, CDP target discovery and attach, screenshot dispatch and disconnect reaping are proven against a fixture CDP server; no real Chrome MV3 extension is loaded.

features.title: Native and client applications

acceptance_evidence.required: Each inventoried client completes protocol-v4 connection and its platform smoke suite.

known_differences: No npm-free Rust implementation or acceptance evidence exists in this repository at this baseline.

features.title: Claude migration provider

acceptance_evidence.required: Plan/apply fixtures cover instructions, MCP servers, skills, memory, credentials, and safe config.

known_differences: Plan and apply are proven against a synthetic Claude home with an injected platform and secret store; JavaScript skills are refused rather than migrated, which is recorded as a deliberate difference.

features.title: Codex migration provider

acceptance_evidence.required: Plan/apply fixtures cover auth, session bindings, source discovery, targets, and sidecars.

known_differences: Auth, session bindings, source discovery, targets and sidecars are proven against synthetic Codex homes; native plugins and hooks are excluded rather than activated, which is recorded as a deliberate difference.

features.title: Hermes migration provider

acceptance_evidence.required: Plan/apply fixtures cover config, models, memory, skills, secrets, credentials, and safe exclusions.

known_differences: Config, models, memory, skills, secrets and credentials are proven against a synthetic Hermes home; plugins and MCP tokens are excluded for manual review rather than migrated, which is recorded as a deliberate difference.
